statement: Under the authorized shares method, the Delaware corporation franchise tax is $175 where authorized capital stock does not exceed 5,000 shares; $250 where it exceeds 5,000 but is not more than 10,000 shares; and a further $85 for each additional 10,000 shares or part thereof (8 Del. C. § 503(a)), subject to the § 503(c) $175 minimum and $200,000 maximum; a Large Corporate Filer (national-exchange-listed and meeting § 503(c)'s consolidated revenue/asset conditions) instead pays $250,000. The Division of Corporations' published examples: 10,005 authorized shares pay $335.00; 100,000 authorized shares pay $1,015.00.
caveat: Amounts change by statute. The Division's annual bill defaults to this method and can often be lowered by recomputing under the assumed par value capital method. The annual report filing fee, the $200 late penalty, interest, and the $5,000+ quarterly-installment rule are separate obligations (rule us-de.franchise-tax-annual-report). Verify against the live statute and agency page before paying or planning.
